lines.text: It’s project time! Simulate a real-world process to answer a question: write rules and assumptions, build it with randomness and agents or time steps, measure a result, and run an experiment by changing one setting.
Pick something real: how a rumour spreads, traffic at a crossing, fish and sharks, rain filling a tank, or dice games.
Write your rules (what each agent or step does) and your assumptions (what you leave out).
A simulation needs a measurement: a counter, a percentage, a population over time.
Use your simulation to answer a question: “What happens if we double the speed?” Change one thing and compare.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now plan it, build it, test it, and share it!
